I have farmed this 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years, and I know what it can bear. At 62, with only two of us in the house and off-farm work to juggle, I cannot afford to chase every new input or tire myself out with extra labor. I keep it simple: wheat in autumn, maize after the wheat comes out in June. The well gives me water when I need it, but electricity costs money, so I irrigate only at the critical times.

For wheat, I will rotary-till the land before sowing and plant improved seed — the same reliable variety my neighbors have used for years. I will spread about 55–60 jin of urea per mu across the season, which comes to roughly 28 kg of nitrogen. I do not buy phosphate or potash; the soil has enough, and compound fertilizer is too expensive for the return I see. I will irrigate three times from the well: at green-up in spring, at jointing, and at heading. I will spray four times for weeds and insects. In a normal year, this wheat should give me about 500 kg per mu.

For maize, I will plant hybrid seed immediately after the wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plough, and at my age I do not have the labor for it, so I will use no-tillage planting to get the crop in fast. The maize gets no extra nitrogen from me — the leftover fertility from the wheat season is enough, and the summer rains help it grow. I will irrigate twice if the dry spells come, and spray three times for pests. I expect about 550 kg per mu.
